title: International Congress of Women at The Hague
summary: From 28 April to 1 May 1915, women from twelve countries met at The Hague during the First World War. UNC records that Dutch suffragist Aletta Jacobs called it and Jane Addams chaired. WILPF counts 1,136 participants. It produced a twelve-point resolution and a committee later renamed the Women's International League for Peace and Freedom.

where.historical_name: The Hague, Kingdom of the Netherlands

importance.justification: A wartime international gathering of women that led to the body now called WILPF.
